Scenario: Session impersonation via weak signing secret or session misuse
Planned_Mitigation: Require strong secret, expiry and server check; verify altered cookie denied

Scenario: Credential stuffing or guessing
Planned_Mitigation: Vetted password hashing and monitoring/throttling

Scenario: Client alters upload metadata or declared size
Planned_Mitigation: Validate lengths and bytes on server

Scenario: User disputes share/delete due to missing event record
Planned_Mitigation: Record actor, object, action, outcome and timestamp

Scenario: Private evidence leaked through direct static path
Planned_Mitigation: Server-only authorized download; private file store

Scenario: IDOR read/share access when object ACL not checked
Planned_Mitigation: Owner and grant checks on each operation

Scenario: Non-owner deletes another investigator’s file
Planned_Mitigation: Owner-only delete and unchanged-data negative test

Scenario: CSRF sensitive grant/revoke/delete
Planned_Mitigation: Anti-CSRF synchronizer token; SameSite; reject missing/wrong token

Scenario: Clickjacking through framed authenticated UI
Planned_Mitigation: CSP frame-ancestors none; XFO DENY

Scenario: Oversized/repeated evidence uploads exhaust disk or worker
Planned_Mitigation: Request maximum, disk cleanup and health check

Scenario: Dynamic SQL query construction allows input manipulation
Planned_Mitigation: Parameterized SQL, negative input test

Scenario: Opaque ID or guessable path leaks evidence metadata
Planned_Mitigation: Generated opaque storage ID and server authorization

Scenario: Native helper memory corruption via unbounded input
Planned_Mitigation: Bounded C input, ASAN and compiler hardening

Scenario: Shell interpretation of upload metadata invokes extra command
Planned_Mitigation: Fixed argv; no shell; allowlist

Scenario: Filename/path traversal writes outside private store
Planned_Mitigation: Opaque server-generated filesystem paths

Scenario: Hash or file byte change not detected
Planned_Mitigation: Ingest digest + recompute before authorized use

Scenario: Mutable local audit table tampered or missing events
Planned_Mitigation: Detailed audit, protected storage; later external immutable archive

Scenario: Logs or traceback expose credentials/evidence
Planned_Mitigation: Error sanitization and log redaction

Scenario: Malformed native-helper data crashes or stalls request
Planned_Mitigation: Process timeout, bounds and controlled error

Scenario: Automated login abuse depletes resources or guesses credentials
Planned_Mitigation: Monitor/rate limit (P1 deployment hardening)

Scenario: Unreviewed GitHub change bypasses security tests
Planned_Mitigation: Require protected branch, PR approval and fail-on-high critical gate

Scenario: Remote plaintext traffic leaks sessions/evidence
Planned_Mitigation: HTTPS before internet exposure

Scenario: Cached authorization persists after revoked share
Planned_Mitigation: Grant state checked at each request

Scenario: Disk/database loss prevents evidence recovery
Planned_Mitigation: Backup and restore drill before production

Scenario: Incorrect retention/delete semantics cause unexpected evidence loss
Planned_Mitigation: Document retention and deletion scope

Scenario: Privileged helper or container magnifies compromise
Planned_Mitigation: Non-root user, minimum capabilities and private writable paths
